title: The DICTO Sunstar
description:
Regular dodecahedra on alternate cubes of a cubic lattice (Euclid's dodecahedron: a cube with a roof on each face) are the densest lattice packing of the dodecahedron [9]; the hole left in each other cube is a star, the Dogstar, and dodecahedra and Dogstars fill space. The Dogstar and this tiling are Hart's [6]. We prove them exactly in ℚ(√5): the Dogstar is the cube minus the six roofs that reach into it, of volume exactly φ/2 at dodecahedron edge 1, and, as a stellation of the dodecahedron (Hart's), we identify it exactly: the dodecahedron 1/φ³ the size of the lattice's, with all 12 pyramids, 24 of the 30 wedges and 8 of the 20 spikes; it lies inside its own cube's stella octangula. The Star Chain Reaction: the great stellated dodecahedron of that core has the cell dodecahedron's 20 corners, and a whole Sunstar (a dodecahedron with the Dogstars on its six faces) 1/φ³ the size fits inside it exactly, with no room to grow, and so on for ever, ratio φ³. DICTO's clusters become single solids: the DICTO Sunstar-Tetra (4 dodecahedra), Sunstar-Octa (6 dodecahedra and the Dogstar that exactly fills their hole: a Sunstar turned inside out) and Sunstar-Rhombi (8 dodecahedra round a sealed Dogstar). Neighbouring dodecahedra touch on exactly one thick Penrose rhombus, the window of the DICTO Jewel [2]; the clusters sit on the Jewel clusters' cells, so their tilings with loose Dogstars (4, 12 and 25 lattices; 2, 1 and 9 up to symmetry) and the octet pattern are those of the Jewel. Eight whole dodecahedra on a 2 × 2 × 2 block make one solid, the DICTO Sunstar-Hexa ((9 + √5)/8 of the block); the space between such blocks is one solid, the DICTO Sunstar-Hexa-Key ((7 − √5)/8: 8 Dogstars and 12 double roofs); they fill space in an irrational ratio, (17 + 4√5)/11, where the Jewel's Hexa and Hexa-Key are 5 : 3. The two lattices have the same cells and roofs: a Jewel is a dodecahedron without its six roof tips, and a stella octangula is a Dogstar with them. All claims are exact except where marked.

The twin of The DICTO Jewel (#41, DICTO DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23496353). Finding #42 on dictospheres.com. Scripts, exact checks and data: https://github.com/DICTOR-Master/kaleidohedra/tree/dc78106/studies/2026-10-20-sunstar, also attached here (dicto-sunstar-study-dc78106.zip).
